comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 published curriculum (later detailed programme not yet determined)
comparator.sourceNotes: Radboud lists ten compulsory 6-EC year-one courses. From year two, students choose Accounting, Finance or International Economics & Policy. This representative route retains the broad economics and policy identity; its year-two path comprises ten listed compulsory 6-EC courses. The applicable year-three route has four compulsory 6-EC specialist courses, four restricted 6-EC electives (24 EC), and a required 12-EC economics thesis. The elective space is explicitly restricted, not invented free electives. The year-three page states that its detail applies through 2026–2027 and later cohorts are not yet determined; this is a comparison of the currently published pathway, not a guaranteed 2028–2029 schedule.

core: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, international markets, strategic choices and empirical economic explanation
Mathematics, statistics, data analysis, applied econometrics and independent economic research

questions: How can economic policy respond to global sustainability challenges and unequal outcomes?
How can businesses remain financially viable while accounting for environmental and social responsibilities?

alternatives.label: Closest match to economics and business economics
alternatives.concept: A quantitative economics and business route linking micro- and macroeconomic theory, econometrics, accounting, finance, firms and international/public policy. Climate and sustainability study informs the economic-policy questions; UCR has less specialist economics depth and no required economics thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The full curriculum contains a substantial economics and methods sequence alongside finance, business, policy and sustainability, so the broad target-relative label fits its actual content.
progression: Introductory economics, entrepreneurship and accounting precede advanced economics, finance and business work. Research methods and mathematics precede econometrics and mathematical statistics; the remaining order respects formal prerequisites and offerings.

alternatives.label: Economic policy, responsible business and sustainability
alternatives.concept: An economics route that asks how governments and businesses respond to climate pressures, unequal outcomes and international rules. It retains theory, accounting, data and econometrics but replaces specialist finance/mathematics/consumer marketing with environmental governance, sociology, political analysis and commercial law.
alternatives.labelReason: The final course set combines eight economics/business courses with policy, social inequality, climate and governance; its label identifies that real combination rather than calling it a sustainability-specialist economics degree.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad route, five actual substitutions replace specialist banking, mathematical statistics, consumer marketing and organisational psychology with commercial regulation, environmental foundations, international politics and social/environmental justice. These choices serve the evidenced policy and responsible-business question, not numerical variety.
progression: Economics and business foundations precede advanced economics and cross-border law; empirical methods precede econometrics. Political foundations precede EU politics, and introductory sociology precedes environmental justice. Formal prerequisites and offered terms pass.

candidates.label: Economic policy, responsible business and sustainability
Finance and financial market stability
candidates.reason: The UCR catalogue offers banking/finance and some related economics, but lacks a sustained specialist financial-markets, instruments, investment and risk sequence for a distinct credible 24-course finance programme. Substituting unrelated business and methods courses would overstate the match.

candidates.label: Accounting and financial reporting
candidates.reason: The current UCR workbook has one accounting and corporate finance course but no advanced financial reporting, management accounting, auditing or control sequence to anchor a separate 24-course accounting route.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target contains three current specialisations. International Economics and Policy covers economic theory, international markets, sustainability, inequality and policy and therefore best represents the degree’s broad academic economics identity. Accounting and Finance are more sector-specific; this choice was made from Radboud’s stated programme, independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

blocks: Economic theory, markets and empirical questions
Both introduce micro and macroeconomic analysis; UCR compresses the range into one course.
Both analyse inflation, growth and macroeconomic policy; UCR approaches these internationally.
Both address consumer choice, markets and strategic behaviour, though UCR is an advanced course.
Both study experimental and behavioural explanations of economic decisions.
Both analyse public spending, market failure and the economics of policy.
No included UCR course directly treats development economics as an economic subfield.
Sociology and public economics touch inequality but do not directly teach labour economics.
General market strategy and behavioural economics do not replace a dedicated game-theory course.
Modern history and business study do not directly teach the disciplinary history of economic thought.
Both teach statistics and basic empirical methods; Radboud embeds these in an economics curriculum.
Both build mathematical techniques used in economic analysis; UCR includes applications beyond economics.
Both apply data analysis in a research project; UCR uses examples across disciplines rather than economics alone.
Both estimate economic relationships with econometric methods; UCR does not provide Radboud’s two-stage sequence.
UCR has one econometrics course aligned to the first applied sequence; no separately credited second stage appears.
Both introduce firm choices and business planning; UCR is more venture-centred and lacks the full finance scope.
Both analyse corporate financial statements and accounting information; UCR is less specialised.
Both examine financial decisions and investment risk, though UCR also covers personal banking.
Both introduce marketing strategy and consumer engagement; UCR develops it as a later elective.
Both examine firm strategy in changing markets; UCR emphasises digital transformation.
The UCR banking/finance course does not separately reproduce international financial policy.
UCR studies environmental governance and impacts, but no scheduled course directly teaches the economics of sustainability at Radboud’s scope.
The UCR macroeconomics course already aligns to Radboud macroeconomics; global business is not a direct substitute for international economic theory.
No single scheduled course covers the advanced topical seminar in international economics and policy as such.
Personal development, specialist electives and thesis
Both develop academic and professional reflection, though UCR personal development has a different focus.
Radboud restricts four six-credit elective choices to its programme list; UCR courses have their own separately represented curriculum.
Radboud requires a twelve-credit economics thesis; UCR independent research appears only as a comparison-only option.

notes.text: Radboud provides a dedicated multi-year economics and business-economics curriculum with a named specialisation, staged econometrics and a required economics thesis. UCR combines its economics, business, quantitative, policy and sustainability courses flexibly, but these programmes do not reproduce Radboud’s disciplinary depth or mandatory thesis.
